citedMandateClauses: 10. Abstain when the proposal is about something these rules do not cover, or when its on-chain actions cannot be matched to its description.
7. Vote against proposals that add new privileged roles, multisigs or upgrade powers, or that weaken timelocks or voting rules.
rationale: The proposal enables Uniswap protocol fees on Arc by registering Arc with the mainnet NTT system, setting Arc as a peer chain, and sending fee-activation calls via Wormhole that set V2 feeTo to TokenJar, transfer V3 factory ownership to a fee adapter, and set the v4 PoolManager fee controller. It is not a treasury transfer, grant, or new risky position, and the mechanism (fee accrual feeding UNI burns) mirrors live deployments on other chains. However, the mandate does not directly address protocol fee activation or cross-chain fee infrastructure, and the on-chain calldata is truncated and cannot be fully matched to the description; the Arc chain is also described as going live in a future date relative to the proposal. Given that the mandate says to abstain when the proposal is outside its rules or cannot be matched to its on-chain actions, abstention is the appropriate call. Some elements (new privileged ownership transfer to adapters and new cross-chain peers) touch rule 7 concerns, which adds uncertainty.
